gold_patch_assessment: The gold patch fully addresses the stated issue: (1) moves keyBindings.ts from config/ to ui/key/, moves keyMatchers.ts and keybindingUtils.ts into ui/key/, moves keyToAnsi.ts from hooks/ to key/; (2) converts KeyBinding from a plain interface to a class with a string-based constructor supporting ctrl+/alt+/shift+/cmd+ modifiers and aliases (option/opt/meta); (3) adds a matches() method on KeyBinding for data-driven key matching; (4) removes the REWIND command (Double Esc) from the Command enum, default bindings, categories, and descriptions; (5) updates all 30+ import sites across UI components, hooks, and scripts to use the new ui/key/ paths; (6) updates the keyboard shortcuts documentation to remove the Double Esc row; (7) converts all defaultKeyBindings entries from object literals to new KeyBinding() calls. The implementation is comprehensive and consistent with every requirement in the issue statement.
base_vs_gold_expectation: On the unmodified base, the tests will fail because: (1) test files at src/ui/key/keyBindings.test.ts, src/ui/key/keyMatchers.test.ts, and src/ui/key/keybindingUtils.test.ts are created by the test patch in a directory that doesn't exist on the base; (2) import paths in the test patch reference ../key/keyMatchers.js and ../key/keybindingUtils.js which don't resolve on the base; (3) the KeyBinding class with string constructor doesn't exist on the base; (4) the REWIND command still exists on the base, causing the metadata completeness tests to fail. After applying the gold patch, all tests should pass: files exist at the expected paths, the KeyBinding class exists with correct parsing, the REWIND command is removed, and all import paths resolve correctly.
too_narrow_risks: The KeyBinding.matches() method is only tested indirectly through the keyMatchers test suite and the useTabbedNavigation integration test. There is no direct unit test for KeyBinding.matches() in keyBindings.test.ts, though the method is exercised thoroughly through the matcher tests.
The removal of the 'double escape' entry from KEY_NAME_MAP in keybindingUtils.ts is not directly tested; it's only caught indirectly if someone tries to format a binding with that key name.
The keyToAnsi.ts file relocation is not explicitly tested (no keyToAnsi tests are run), though the ShellInputPrompt component that imports it would break at build time if the path were wrong.
too_broad_risks: The useTabbedNavigation.test.ts change removes mocks of useKeyMatchers and the Command mock, requiring the real key matching infrastructure to work. This means the test depends on the full chain (KeyBinding class -> defaultKeyBindings -> createKeyMatchers -> defaultKeyMatchers -> useKeyMatchers hook), which could reject an alternative implementation that structures the matcher pipeline differently while still achieving the same observable behavior.
The eval.sh runs npm run build before tests, which compiles the entire project. A build failure in an unrelated module could cause the tests to fail.
implementation_coupling: The test patch replaces object literal key bindings (e.g., { key: 'h', ctrl: true }) with new KeyBinding('ctrl+h') in keyMatchers.test.ts and keybindingUtils.test.ts, coupling tests to the specific KeyBinding class constructor API rather than just testing observable behavior.

The useTabbedNavigation.test.ts removes mocks and relies on the real useKeyMatchers() hook returning real defaultKeyMatchers, coupling that test to the gold patch's module structure and internal wiring.
environment_risks: The eval.sh runs npm run build before tests, which could fail due to unresolved dependencies, TypeScript version issues, or build toolchain problems in the Docker environment.
The test patch applies via git apply or patch --fuzz=5, which could fail if surrounding context lines differ from what the patch expects.

evidence.detail: Issue requires: (1) unify key bindings under ui/key module, (2) KeyBinding class with string constructor, (3) exports of Command/KeyBinding/KeyBindingConfig/defaultKeyBindings/commandCategories/commandDescriptions, (4) modifier parsing (ctrl/alt/shift/cmd), (5) formatting compatibility, (6) key matching via KeyBinding objects, (7) UI imports from unified location, (8) Double Esc no longer treated as regular command.

Gold patch moves 3 files (keyBindings.ts, keyMatchers.ts, keybindingUtils.ts) to ui/key/, creates new keyToAnsi.ts in ui/key/, converts KeyBinding from interface to class, removes REWIND command, updates 30+ import sites, and updates documentation.

Test patch: deletes old keyBindings.test.ts, creates new ui/key/keyBindings.test.ts with KeyBinding constructor tests (12 test cases), renames and updates keyMatchers.test.ts and keybindingUtils.test.ts, updates import paths in 4 existing test files, removes mocks from useTabbedNavigation.test.ts to use real implementations.
Confirmed base repo has KeyBinding as plain interface (not class) at old location, with REWIND command present in enum, bindings, categories, and descriptions.
Confirmed base repo has keyMatchers.ts at old location with standalone matchKeyBinding function, not on a class.

Runs 7 test files covering: keyBindings, keyMatchers, keybindingUtils (all at new ui/key/ paths), plus useSuspend, useTabbedNavigation, InputPrompt, and ExitPlanModeDialog tests for import path validation.

summary: This is a well-constructed benchmark instance. The gold patch comprehensively addresses every requirement in the issue: file relocation to ui/key/, KeyBinding class with string parsing, REWIND removal, import path updates, and formatting/matching compatibility. The test suite covers the KeyBinding constructor (12 test cases for modifiers, aliases, case-insensitivity, errors), config completeness (all commands have bindings, descriptions, categories), key matcher behavior (40+ command matching tests with custom configs), formatting utilities (9 test cases across 4 platforms), and integration tests via real (unmocked) key matching in useTabbedNavigation. Tests would clearly fail on the unmodified base and pass with the gold patch. Minor risks: tests are slightly coupled to the KeyBinding class API (using new KeyBinding() in test data) and the useTabbedNavigation test relies on real implementations end-to-end, but these are reasonable given the issue requirements.
